context: Approved architecture keeps financial mutation logic in one service boundary and uses PostgreSQL as the transactional system of record.
decision: Use a Next.js web app, one modular NestJS API, Supabase PostgreSQL/Auth, and a shared worker for Release 1.

context: The fast path reduces normal webhook latency while durable PostgreSQL work and scheduled recovery preserve processing without a second queue service.
decision: Use PostgreSQL-owned outbox/jobs with immediate bounded processing and a five-minute Cloudflare recovery trigger invoking the same handler.

context: Approved scope excludes live funds and prevents mandatory spend, paid add-ons, PAYG, and automatic upgrades.
decision: Keep all provider activity in PayMongo test mode and require zero-cost infrastructure plans.

context: Machine-exact transitions enable exhaustive tests, while separate payment and refund types prevent ambiguous state interpretation.
decision: Use exact payment-state enum transitions and a separate RefundState enum.

context: The installed runtime is Node 22.14 and the dependency graph must reproduce consistently across local work and CI.
decision: Pin the workspace to Node 22 and pnpm 10.30.3 with a committed lockfile and strict TypeScript checks.

context: Docker engine was unavailable and the existing system PostgreSQL credentials were not usable; project data must remain isolated.
decision: Use a project-owned PostgreSQL 17 cluster bound only to 127.0.0.1 on port 55432 for local verification.

context: Phase 01 establishes schema ownership without allowing silent edits to an already applied migration.
decision: Apply ordered SQL migrations under a PostgreSQL advisory lock and transaction, and verify applied migration checksums.

context: The portfolio must not require a paid image processing service or add unnecessary serverless image optimization requests.
decision: Serve the landing page artwork as local static images without Next.js image optimization.

context: The generated artwork was over 2.8 MB combined, while the public page serves it directly as static files to avoid runtime optimization.
decision: Resize and compress the local diagram and footer art during implementation; keep static runtime delivery without a hosted image optimizer.

context: The owner selected a public solo GitHub workflow with merge commits, no required second human approval, and independently reviewed financial changes; Windows and Linux CI must see the same text bytes.
decision: Use personal/defnotwig → dev → staging → main PR promotion, exact-base/diff Codex review evidence, merge commits only, MIT licensing, and LF line endings for tracked text.

context: The approved solo PR workflow requires auditable CI and independent review evidence while preserving merge commits and preventing routine administrator bypass.
decision: Protect dev, staging, and main with PRs, verify and review-evidence checks, resolved conversations, enforced admin rules, and disabled force pushes and branch deletion; keep linear history disabled.

context: GitHub Actions reported that ubuntu-latest was about to move to Ubuntu 26 and that older action runtimes were being forced onto Node 24, so a time-stable and supported CI runtime is preferable.
decision: Pin CI to ubuntu-24.04 and immutable Node 24-compatible actions/checkout v7.0.1 and actions/setup-node v7.1.0 SHAs; keep application verification on Node 22.14.0.

context: GitHub removed the Node 20 action runtime on 2026-09-23, and pnpm/action-setup v4 still declared node20 despite having succeeded under temporary runner compatibility behavior.
decision: Replace pnpm/action-setup v4 with immutable v6.1.0 SHA ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 so every JavaScript action in CI declares the Node 24 runtime.
Keep PR titles as plain Conventional Commit subjects and require exactly one trailing PR-number token on GitHub merge subjects.
context: The live PR #1 merge showed that GitHub automatically appends the PR number when merge_commit_title is PR_TITLE; requiring the number in the title duplicates it. CI now rejects duplicate tokens to prevent recurrence.

decision: Allow one exact legacy merge commit with a duplicated PR number while requiring exact one-suffix merge subjects everywhere else.
context: The PR #1 merge at SHA 3c62834af3160c5b1e212e02b2e04b8b316c98a8 already exists in published history and appears in the dev-to-staging promotion range. Rewriting it would violate history preservation; the SHA and subject allowlist preserves promotion CI while PR-title validation prevents recurrence.

PayMo qualification audit found self-issued/header-based identity, placeholder provider acceptance, fabricated card state, absent durable workers and missing database-enforced financial invariants. User approved in-place sandbox API correction and narrowly scoped dependencies; all implementation branches are isolated for review.
decision: Use Supabase Auth with server-verified JWT and database memberships; separate local fixtures from real provider mode; enforce transaction, ledger, reservation and claim-token invariants in PostgreSQL; introduce only pinned and reasoned qualification dependencies; never represent simulation as provider or hosted proof.

context: The preceding qualification decision line used the client calendar date while recording UTC, producing a future timestamp. This append-only correction preserves that original line and records its actual time basis.
decision: Use the execution clock for future decision timestamps; the qualification decision was made at 2026-10-18T14:28:26Z.
Allow only the three PayMo qualification codex branches to submit reviewed pull requests into personal/defnotwig and run the existing CI and independent review-evidence checks on that target.
context: The user requested isolated specialist branches be integrated through reviewed pull requests before the normal personal-to-dev-to-staging-to-main release flow. The previous policy excluded personal as a PR target and would reject arbitrary codex branches.

decision: Persist worker claim tokens and require a live matching token for completion or failure; reconcile payment success only from matching verified provider observations.
context: Concurrency qualification showed worker identity alone does not fence expired owners, and state-only reconciliation can bypass the payment source guard or rely on stale local attempt state.

decision: Enforce multi-currency balanced debits and credits per transaction and currency in LedgerService, and expand concurrency test suites across payments, webhook storms, out-of-order transitions, refund capacity competition, lease fencing, and repeated reconciliation.
context: Auditing financial mutation invariants revealed that multi-currency ledger lines required per-currency debit/credit validation in application code alongside PostgreSQL constraint triggers, and all concurrency race conditions required deterministic test verification.
